# Loan Origination Assistant — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Loan Origination Assistant
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 20 captured build checkpoints; 5 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 5 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness. Building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved lending environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded lending files, proposed lending systems, Microsoft Teams and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger. Record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the loan-origination system, borrower data, verification services, document repository and Teams approvals. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare loan-officer, processor, underwriter, closing and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview, not publication. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files, with no PAC CLI or YAML import. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Lending rule ownership | Have authorized lending owners replace the fictional criteria, rates, document requirements and conditions before customer data is used. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** How applications, borrower documents, conditions and closing timelines are coordinated before a lending decision. Establish current preparation effort before crediting the agent, without weakening fair-lending controls or delegated authority.

Fill your baseline record:

| Application | Product | Stage | Measurement period | Missing documents | Open conditions | Handoffs | Decision owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree lending replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Lending business owner | Approve lending sources, preparation scope and escalation workflow; agree production success measures without treating synthetic files as results. |
| Authorized lending reviewers | Own eligibility, credit, fair-lending, compliance, disclosure, closing and funding decisions outside the agent. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and five skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing and capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any lending connection is approved. |
| Lending system connection owners | Approve least-privilege references for the loan-origination system, borrower data, verification services and document repository. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check LOA-01 through LOA-05 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; fail any response claiming to approve, execute or submit. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route lending decisions to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Lending replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The lending owner records how applications, documents, conditions and closing timelines are coordinated today before choosing measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/loan-origination-assistant/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for borrower and application data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/loan-origination-assistant/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/loan-origination-assistant/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/loan-origination-assistant/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/loan-origination-assistant/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Loan Origination Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_loan-origination-assistant-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_loan-origination-assistant-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_application-review_01
9. Add skill: aibast_condition-tracking_05
10. Add skill: aibast_credit-analysis_02
11. Add skill: aibast_decision-recommendation_04
12. Add skill: aibast_document-verification_03
13. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
14. Open a fresh Preview conversation
15. Pass LOA-01: Loan Officer
16. Pass LOA-02: Underwriter
17. Pass LOA-03: Processor
18. Pass LOA-04: Senior Underwriter
19. Pass LOA-05: Closing Coordinator
20. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: LOA-01, LOA-02, LOA-03, LOA-04, LOA-05. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `LoanOriginationAssistantAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The optional Brainstem lane is recorded as used or skipped; no workshop step depends on it.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, five skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged lending prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full response; annotated screenshots do not replace the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before showing borrower or application data. Request only read scopes for approved lending systems and documents. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved loan-origination system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending system connection owners

1. **Bind Approved loan-origination system — read:** Bind approved read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Approved loan-origination system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved loan-origination system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved loan-origination system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Clear no condition and promise no closing date; list the open conditions for the closing authority. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report that no record exists; never substitute another application.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Dynamics 365 borrower or relationship data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending system connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 borrower or relationship data — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 borrower or relationship data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 borrower or relationship data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 borrower or relationship data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Browse nothing and call no bureau or verification service; use only the packaged snapshot. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, verification or lending action succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Approved lending verification services

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending system connection owners

1. **Bind Approved lending verification services — read:** Bind least-privilege read-only verification actions.

2. **Identity for Approved lending verification services:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved lending verification services:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved lending verification services:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Browse nothing and call no bureau or verification service; use only the packaged snapshot. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, verification or lending action succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Controlled document repository

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending system connection owners

1. **Bind Controlled document repository — read:** Add approved document sources as knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for Controlled document repository:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Controlled document repository:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Controlled document repository:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Give no lending or financial advice; provide the evidence and name the authorized reviewer. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, verification or lending action succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams underwriting approvals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending system connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams underwriting approvals — write:** Gate any approval request behind an authorized workflow (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams underwriting approvals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams underwriting approvals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams underwriting approvals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Approve and send nothing; give nonbinding findings for authorized underwriting review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return findings or conditions and name the authorized reviewer; execute nothing.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending system connection owners

Create only approved least-privilege references, read-only first, with explicit approval gates for consequential actions.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Only approved least-privilege tools exist, with explicit approval gates for consequential actions and unresolved connector work documented.
- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no live lookup or lending action is claimed without tool evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Before rollout, test an approved test deployment as loan officers, processors, underwriters and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data measures; fictional criteria, rates and ratios are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked lending corpus | All five cases, LOA-01 through LOA-05, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, five skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Lending authority boundary | Any eligibility decision, approval, denial, pricing, lock, disclosure, condition clearance, closing or funding is no-go. |
| Unknown identifiers | Unknown identifiers are rejected; a substituted or invented record is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a positive target-state anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required images. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Lending business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved lending audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed lending sessions, their transcripts, tool connection and authentication errors, and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
